title: Minimum Height Trees
summary: You may choose any vertex as the root of the given undirected tree.

contractDetails.constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 20000. Vertices use labels 0 through n−1. There are n−1 distinct undirected edges, with no self-loops, and they form a tree.
contractDetails.output-checking: Compare a unique set of zero-based minimum-height roots. Root order is irrelevant.

statement: You may choose any vertex as the root of the given undirected tree. Its height is the longest distance from that root to another vertex. Return every root that achieves the smallest possible height, in any order.

examples.explanation: Both middle vertices minimize the longest distance.
The only vertex is the only root.
The star center reaches each leaf in one edge.

constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 20000. Vertices use labels 0 through n−1. There are n−1 distinct undirected edges, with no self-loops, and they form a tree.
hints: Conceptual: A minimum-height root is at the center of the tree.
Directional: Remove all leaves in rounds.
Implementation: Track current degrees and enqueue vertices when they become leaves. Stop when at most two vertices remain.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
